correctness.rationale: The shift-square restriction over a substitution phase has exact abelian cocycle \((1,1-z_0)\). Nested period-doubling cylinders have precisely the two return words \(\Gamma^{n-1}(1)\), \(\Gamma^n(1)\), proved by induction using recognizability of even indices. Their integer increment matrix has determinant of magnitude \(2^{n-1}\) and an odd entry, hence Smith form \(\operatorname{diag}(1,2^{n-1})\). The finite-group extension decomposes into finitely many clopen minimal sets; their translation stabilizer coincides with the stabilized return subgroup, by future-dependence of component labels and minimal recurrence. Therefore exactly \(2^{\nu_2(\kappa)}\) components exist, each with \(\kappa^2/2^{\nu_2(\kappa)}\) points over each base point. The in-package finite checker validates small returns and indices but cannot substitute for these infinite steps.

originality.rationale: Kang--Jaeger (arXiv:2609.01140v1), Theorem 1.7/Proposition 4.10, gives binary minimal versus nonminimal classification for this family; its decomposition and rank lemmas do not compute number or common ranks at even modulus. A finite Smith index and a dynamical stabilizer equality are needed to deduce the exact arithmetic decomposition. Published semantic-record searches for valuation, equivalent skew cocycle, component counts, ranks and return permutations found no equal or broader statement. Residual equivalence under older finite-odometer cocycle terminology is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The focal 2026 paper naturally asks how a nonminimal permutative lift decomposes and defines fibre rank. This exact answer classifies two intrinsic invariants for all even moduli: the number is the entire two-primary factor of the modulus, and every piece has the same rank. The unbounded component-count spectrum and stabilizer-index mechanism are more than an isolated finite test or a routine restatement of nonminimality. It also identifies what structural information is lost when a binary minimal/nonminimal criterion is the only output.
